criteria.title: Forced failed subgoal and verified recovery
criteria.scope: Public-pass to forced domain-fail to an accepted revision of that failed target to independent final-pass, in at least one adaptive trace per family.
limitations: Forced certification invalidation and a domain failure are reported separately; one does not imply the other.
Pre-fault success is checked with public gates only; hidden final grading is deliberately not queried before the fault or fed back for repair.
Observed recovery demonstrates a finite trace; it does not establish comparative efficacy or uniform reliability.

criteria.title: Hierarchy, state transitions, and before/after replans
criteria.scope: Successfully replayed hierarchical checkpoints plus an exercised, failure-evidenced accepted replan.
limitations: Replay checks the recorded state and diagnosis provenance; it does not certify the semantic truth of model-written causal explanations.
Hash chains detect checked inconsistencies, not wholesale forgery by a writer able to regenerate the entire record.

criteria.title: Immutable root contract
criteria.scope: Every scheduled trace was replayed and the root contract stayed identical in root-bearing state and request snapshots.
limitations: Zero explicit edit requests does not exercise rejection of a root edit; mutation rejection is a separate adversarial software test.
Syntactic edit-request counts do not infer a model's intent.

criteria.title: Observed coverage across different task families
criteria.scope: Complete replayed outcomes across all three declared synthetic task families; failures remain in coverage.
limitations: Coverage includes unsuccessful trials and is not a success claim.
Three selected synthetic families do not establish broad real-world task generalization.

criteria.title: Unrelated goals and artifact fields preserved
criteria.scope: Plan comparisons cover accepted adaptive revisions; artifact comparisons cover audited adaptive fault paths independently of whether a revision was accepted. Both comparison sets must be nonempty.
limitations: Zero unrelated comparisons is UNCERTAIN, never a vacuous locality PASS.
Locality is defined by the declared task dependencies and artifact ownership, not inferred semantic independence.

criteria.title: Failure-evidenced and bounded replanning
criteria.scope: A replan request must have current failed-leaf evidence and authorization; attempted requests stay within the declared cap.
limitations: Operational necessity means satisfying the declared failure/progress predicate; it does not prove each replan improves outcomes or is globally optimal.
Attempts count issued replan requests, including failed or over-budget requests, and may exceed accepted plus rejected replies.

criteria.title: Independent final grading and replay
criteria.scope: Audited final grades must match terminal claims; noncandidate budget failures need not call the hidden grader.
limitations: Replay and hidden grading establish agreement with the implemented evaluator, not absence of evaluator bugs.
Self-reported success and changed tests cannot substitute for this evidence.

criteria.title: Scale coverage and finite resilience
criteria.scope: Engineering covers the varied observed trees; the separate finite live-data rule tests frozen per-setting success, paired stress drop, and observed locality thresholds.
limitations: Requested depth counts levels including the root; measured max_depth_edges counts edges from root zero.
Deeper scale fixtures add executable certification leaves. Depth is not varied at fixed leaf count or fixed work.
The selected scale settings are not a full factorial design; marginal and interaction effects are not identified generally.
Distinct scale settings generated from shared source instances need not be independent task draws. No scale CI or significance test is reported.
Thresholds are frozen design choices, not estimates from these outcomes. With six assigned adaptive fault trials per setting, a 0.80 threshold requires at least five successes.
The stress contrast jointly changes size, depth, and direct dependency burden; fault targets may also differ across paired settings. It is not an isolated causal scale effect.
The six pairs reuse three source tasks across two repeats; no independent-Bernoulli or population reliability claim is made.
A failed path without a repair remains a failure in the success denominator and supplies no positive artifact-locality evidence.

criteria.title: Finite repeatability and scientific stability uncertainty
criteria.scope: Engineering covers repeated outcome reporting; the separate live reliability rule requires every adaptive task/condition cell to meet frozen success and integrity thresholds.
limitations: No population power, precision, or future-stability guarantee establishes that the repeat count is scientifically sufficient; a finite acceptance threshold is a separate claim.
Repeated calls of one task are dependent observations within the same task cluster.
Deterministic oracle repetitions do not estimate model stochasticity or empirical stability.
